terms.gloss: a ceremony, a solemn rite or festival
terms.comment: The neuter of sollemnis “yearly, established, solemn”: any formal ceremony, sacred or civic, as Livy uses it. Lewis & Short notes it is perhaps not in Cicero, who says sollemnia sacra, lūdī sollemnēs.

terms.gloss: a religious ceremony, a sacred rite
terms.comment: Only of worship, mostly in the plural; in the singular more often reverence or sanctity.

terms.gloss: a rite; the manner of a ceremony
evidence: Liv. 1.7: sacra dīs aliīs Albānō rītū, Graecō Herculī facit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The form a rite follows, the way it is done (Graecō rītū), and so “custom” in general (rītū, in the manner of).
Late Latin, as in the Church’s solemnities.

phrases.latin: inter pūblicum sollemne spōnsālibus rīte factīs
phrases.english: the betrothal was duly made at a public ceremony

sources: Lewis & Short: sollemnis · Lewis & Short: caerimonia · Lewis & Short: ritus
